summary: First iteration end-to-end testing of Retail ERP. Backend: 23/23 pytest cases passed (100%) covering auth, role enforcement, employees CRUD, attendance manual/group/today/list, leaves apply+decision, shifts list/assign, payroll generate+payslip-PDF, dashboard stats, CSV report. Frontend: Login → Operations Dashboard with all 6 KPIs and 3 charts renders correctly. Sidebar nav (Dashboard/Employees/Attendance/Leaves/Shifts/Payroll/Reports) shown for admin. Employees page seeds 6 employees (Priya/Ramesh/Anita/Suresh/Neha/Arjun). Attendance Group Check-In simulated face recognition modal opens, animates scan overlay, surfaces 3 recognized employees with bounding labels, Mark Check-In button visible. Shifts shows 3 shift cards with counts (Morning:3, Afternoon:2, Night:1) and roster with reassign dropdown. Payroll Generate button works and table populates with employee rows. Reports page exposes Export CSV. Logout returns to /login. Employee role (priya@dmart.co): lands on My Workspace with profile, KPIs, latest attendance; sidebar correctly hides admin-only links (Employees/Shifts/Reports); directly visiting /employees as employee redirects to /. Role enforcement verified server-side (403 on admin endpoints).

minor.issue: date_to is hardcoded to {month_key}-31 which works as string-compare upper-bound but is semantically incorrect for months <31 days; current impl is benign because attendance.date strings never exceed real month length, but consider using calendar.monthrange for correctness.
Approving a leave decrements leave_balance unconditionally with no lower-bound check; balance can go negative.

backend/.env CORS_ORIGINS='*' combined with allow_credentials=True is technically invalid per CORS spec (browsers will reject credentialed requests with wildcard origin). Works here because frontend uses Bearer header fallback, but should be restricted to explicit origins for production.

ui_bugs.issue: Modal close (X) button has no data-testid and Escape key does not close the modal; e2e tests have to click the X or Cancel manually. Add data-testid='scan-modal-close' and bind Esc.

issues: Visually appropriate retail aisle image; copy and CTA contrast are good.
Charts (Recharts) render with good contrast; KPI cards uniform; no contrast/spacing issues observed.

action_items: (LOW) Add data-testid='scan-modal-close' on the Group Check-In modal X button and add Escape-key handler.
(LOW) Clamp leave_balance to 0 minimum when approving leave decisions.
(LOW) Use calendar.monthrange for payroll date_to upper bound.
(INFO) Tighten CORS_ORIGINS to explicit production origins when deploying.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~910 lines — close to the 700 LOC threshold; consider splitting into routers (auth, employees, attendance, leaves, shifts, payroll, reports) for maintainability.
Bcrypt + JWT auth implemented correctly (httpOnly cookie + Bearer fallback). Cookie has secure=False which is fine for the preview environment but should be True in production over HTTPS.
MongoDB ObjectId is properly excluded via {'_id': 0} projections throughout.
All endpoints use Pydantic models; admin-only endpoints gated with require_admin dependency.
Group attendance correctly upserts and avoids duplicate check-ins; method='face_recognition' recorded for traceability.
Seed admin re-syncs password if changed in .env — good idempotency.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all flows verified, one minor modal-close UX gap)

seed_data_creation: Seeded automatically on backend startup: 1 admin + 6 demo employees with linked employee user logins. Tests do not modify seeded data; ephemeral TEST_ employees are created+deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All backend endpoints validated and frontend flows pass. If main agent fixes the modal close UX, just re-run the existing pytest suite (`pytest /app/backend/tests/test_erp_api.py -v`) and a single Playwright pass on Attendance + Group Check-In modal. Payroll PDF download was verified by both backend (PDF magic bytes) and is downloadable via row PDF button in UI.
rca of the issue: No blocking issues found. The minor frontend modal-close gap is a UX/testing affordance issue, not functional — modal can still be dismissed via the visible X button and Cancel button; only the keyboard shortcut + data-testid are missing.
